questionText: Describe how the plain rice is boiled.
modelAnswer:
Method 1: Put water in a saucepan with a lid and place on fire to boil. Pick and wash rice, then pour into boiling water. Add salt, stir, cover, and allow to cook for 15-20 minutes until soft. Reduce heat to lower temperature and leave rice to become grainy.
Method 2: Pick and wash rice. Put rice, cold water, and salt in a saucepan with a lid and place on fire to boil. Stir, cover, allow to cook, check after 15-20 minutes to see if soft, reduce heat, and leave to become grainy.
Method 3: Wash the rice cooker bowl. Measure quantity of rice needed into the bowl. Add measured amount of water (twice the quantity of rice). Switch on rice cooker, press the cook button, leave to cook, and switch off when cooked.

questionText: State two changes observed in the rice after it has been boiled.
modelAnswer:
1. Colour changes from light cream to white/attractive.
2. The grains soften/become soft when cooked (texture changes) and there is an increase in quantity.

questionText: Outline the steps to be followed in the preparation of the syrup for the fruit salad.
modelAnswer:
1. Dissolve a measured amount of sugar in a measured amount of water (100 g of sugar to 250 ml of water).
2. Bring to the boil.
3. Boil for 5 minutes till sticky.
4. Remove from fire and cool.
5. Chill and use.

questionText: State two reasons why she should garnish the food to be served.
modelAnswer:
1. For visual appeal / to enhance appearance / for attraction.
2. To enhance/improve flavour, whet appetite, or add variety to texture.

questionText: State three suitable food items that can be used to garnish plain rice at the buffet party.
modelAnswer:
1. Carrots (julienne or thinly sliced sautéed)
2. Sprig of parsley / Green peas / Sweet corn
3. Sliced cucumber / Sliced tomato / Sweet pepper

questionText: Aunty Mary uses charcoal as fuel for cooking at home. Give two reasons to convince her to use liquefied Petroleum Gas (L.P.G.) instead of charcoal.
modelAnswer:
1. LP Gas is cleaner to use and environmentally friendly (prevents deforestation).
2. It is convenient, time-saving, labour/energy-saving, and easier to control than charcoal.

questionText: State two functions of a table cloth in table setting.
modelAnswer:
1. It protects the table from scratches, stains, and spills.
2. It decorates the table and enhances its appearance (or conceals an ugly surface).

questionText: Akosua felt unwell after eating waakye from the school canteen. The doctor confirmed it was food poisoning. List four signs and symptoms she exhibited.
modelAnswer:
1. Vomiting
2. Stomach ache / cramps / pains / upset
3. Diarrhoea
4. Headache (or fever / high temperature / nausea / general body weakness)

questionText: Araba cut some fruits to prepare the family's favourite fruit salad but found out that the colour of the cut bananas had changed after an hour. Describe what caused the change in colour.
modelAnswer: When the banana is cut, its inner surface is exposed. The exposed surface containing certain enzymes/chemicals reacts with atmospheric oxygen (oxidation). This enzymatic browning turns the exposed surface brown, making it visually unattractive.

questionText: Kwame realizes that the mother's pot of rice has become slimy the next morning. State one cause of the spoilage.
modelAnswer: Contamination by bacteria (or contamination by moulds / exposure to warmth).

questionText: Safe substances are used for preserving different types of foods. List one safe substance for preserving each of the following foods: (i) fresh fish, (ii) fruits, (iii) onion.
modelAnswer:
(i) Fresh fish: Salt (or vinegar)
(ii) Fruits: Sugar
(iii) Onion: Vinegar

questionText: State two ways of finishing the edge of a plain seam.
modelAnswer:
1. Pinking
2. Edge stitching / machining (or overcastting / overlocking / blanket stitching)

questionText: Re-arrange the following operations for preparing the tenon in sequential order: I. cut off the wastes on the sides of the tenon; II. prepare the workpiece to the required dimensions; III. clean the workpiece with the appropriate tool; IV. measure and cut the workpiece; V. mark-out to the required sizes; VI. hold the workpiece firmly in position and cut the sides of the tenon.
modelAnswer:
1. II (Prepare the workpiece to the required dimensions)
2. IV (Measure and cut the workpiece)
3. V (Mark-out to the required sizes)
4. VI (Hold the workpiece firmly in position and cut the sides of the tenon)
5. I (Cut off the wastes on the sides of the tenon)
6. III (Clean the workpiece with the appropriate tool)

questionText: List two tools for preparing the tenon.

questionText: List two adhesives for assembling the joint.

questionText: State one reason why safety must be observed in the workshop when making the joint.

questionText: Give one importance of appraising the tenon produced.

questionText: Copy and complete Table 1: (i) Building site, (ii) Wood workshop, (iii) Metal workshop.
modelAnswer:
(i) Building site: One measuring tool = Surveyor's tape / Tape measure / Folding rule. One marking out tool = Profile board / Peg / Chalk / Builder's square / Line and pins.
(ii) Wood workshop: One measuring tool = Rule / Tape measure / Folding rule. One marking out tool = Pencil / Try square / Marking gauge / Mortise gauge / Marking knife.
(iii) Metal workshop: One measuring tool = Steel rule / Vernier caliper / Micrometer screw gauge / Tape measure. One marking out tool = Scriber / Centre punch / Dot punch / Pair of dividers / Odd leg calipers.

questionText: Make a freehand pictorial sketch of the centre punch.
modelAnswer: A freehand pictorial sketch of a cylindrical metal tool with a knurled body and a tapered tip pointed at an included angle of 90 degrees.

questionText: Indicate the point angle of the centre punch sketched in (b)(i).
State one use of the centre punch.
modelAnswer: It is used for locating the centre of a hole to be drilled (or for correcting an off-centred position of a hole to be drilled).

questionText: State one finish suitable for each of the following products: (i) plastered block wall, (ii) metal gate, (iii) wooden wardrobe.

questionText: In designing and making a kitchen stool, which saw would be appropriate for cutting a given length of wood: (i) across the grain, (ii) along the grain?

(ii) Along the grain: Rip saw

questionText: State two suitable materials each used for joining a: (i) wooden top to a metal base, (ii) plastic top to a wooden base.

(ii) Plastic top to a wooden base: Adhesives / Screws / Brackets / Angle plates
